card: Escapes backslashes before double quotes when sending -torpassword in the Tor control port AUTHENTICATE command under HASHEDPASSWORD authentication. Currently, Bitcoin Core only escapes quotation marks, which causes Tor's control-spec parser to interpret backslashes as escape characters, corrupting passwords containing backslashes and causing Tor authentication and onion service setup to fail. The author tested against Tor 0.4.9.12, confirming that authentication fails on master with backslashes in the password and succeeds with this patch.
changed_since_previous: None; the change and test remain identical.
evidence: Author verification against Tor 0.4.9.12 with HashedControlPassword: 'on master bitcoind logs "tor: Authentication failed", with this change authentication succeeds and ADD_ONION creates the onion service.'
problem: When authenticating to Tor using `HASHEDPASSWORD`, Bitcoin Core wraps the password in quotes and escapes double quotes, but not backslashes. Because Tor parses the argument as a control-spec QuotedString, unescaped backslashes are interpreted as escape characters, altering the password or escaping the closing quote and failing authentication.

risk.why: A mistake in escaping could cause Tor control port authentication to fail, preventing the node from registering its onion service.

summary: Escapes backslashes in `-torpassword` before escaping double quotes when authenticating to the Tor control port with `HASHEDPASSWORD`. It also adds a functional test asserting the formatted `AUTHENTICATE` command using a mock Tor control server.
